query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a controlled amount of aluminum (Al) to the CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy will promote the in‐situ formation of a lubricious Al2O3 tribo‐film during sliding, thereby maintaining a low coefficient of friction and wear rate from room temperature up to 800 °C.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy as originally tested.
generation.intervention: Introduce a controlled Al alloying addition to modify the composition to a CoCrFeNiAl system.
generation.conditions: Sliding wear tests performed in ambient air, under the same load and sliding conditions as the baseline evaluation, while progressively increasing the temperature from room temperature to 800 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: An in-situ formed, continuous Al2O3 oxide layer at the sliding interface.
generation.mechanism: At elevated temperatures, the added Al segregates to the surface and oxidizes to form a thin, continuous Al2O3 film that provides lubrication. This scale reduces friction and wear, while at lower temperatures the modified microstructure retains the inherent high-entropy alloy toughness and wear resistance. The self-adaptive formation of the oxide layer thus mediates sliding performance across the full temperature range.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the unmodified CoCrFeNi alloy, the CoCrFeNiAl alloy is expected to exhibit a consistently lower coefficient of friction and reduced wear rate across the entire temperature regime.
generation.baseline: Sliding performance (coefficient of friction and wear rate) of the unmodified CoCrFeNi alloy under the specified test conditions.
generation.boundary: Temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C, the same contact load and ambient air environment as used in the baseline tests.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty regarding the degree and stability of the in-situ generated Al2O3 film over the full temperature range and under cyclic sliding conditions. The interplay between low-temperature deformation mechanisms and high-temperature oxidation in the modified alloy also remains to be experimentally validated.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of baseline CoCrFeNi alloy specimens and one set of modified CoCrFeNiAl specimens with a controlled Al addition. Perform systematic sliding wear tests at room temperature, intermediate temperatures, and up to 800 °C under identical loads and environmental conditions. Subsequently, analyze surface morphology and chemical composition of the wear tracks using SEM, TEM, XPS, and/or Raman spectroscopy.
measurements: Wear rate (mass loss or volume loss)
Surface oxide layer characterization (thickness, continuity, phase identification)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the CoCrFeNiAl alloy does not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in both the coefficient of friction and wear rate relative to the baseline CoCrFeNi alloy across the tested temperature range, or if no continuous Al2O3 tribo-film is detected on the worn surfaces at high temperatures.
